<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via isOverrideActor (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `68ad15ef87bed8533de0440c4d2a2e0daa1fa1a4` — the merge of head `f89aa1cf9e8eac7f80d99a8f7de0c39df065732a` into base `7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 68ad15ef87bed8533de0440c4d2a2e0daa1fa1a4 && git checkout 68ad15ef87bed8533de0440c4d2a2e0daa1fa1a4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca f89aa1cf9e8eac7f80d99a8f7de0c39df065732a && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca && git merge --no-ff f89aa1cf9e8eac7f80d99a8f7de0c39df065732a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the record below. An isolated reviewer rendered it on this head at the contract-review tier.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `350bc40b6e86baf76d6342c26b96d63a3f9311c0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-act-doors-read-visibility.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/pending-approver-read-grant.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-column-creation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/pre-18-tenant-column.testkit.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md (all read on `main` or at the head, none reviewed)

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change comes from one predicate, `ApprovalService.isOverrideActor`. Every caller of it was read at the head.

- **Override doors (approve, reject, recall, reassign): right.** A tenant administrator acting on a request with no organization under `group` or `isolated` moves from admitted to `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`. The refusal comes from `refuseUnreadableRequest`, before any status, slate or submitter test.
- **Other act doors (send back, resubmit, remind, request info, comment): right.** The same caller used to pass the readability check through the override and get the door's own answer. It now gets the missing-id answer.
- **`viewer.can_override`: right.** It uses the same predicate on the row's organization, so the flag and the gate still agree.
- **The three callers that pass the actor's own organization (`visibleRequestIdsFor`, `visibleRequestIds`, the pending-approver read grant): right in direction, undeclared.** A tenant-administrator context with no active organization under a wall moves from the unrestricted view to the participant set. See ③ and ④.
- **`single`: unchanged, right.** `postureEnforcesWall('single')` is false, so the tenant arm still admits. This is pinned on the four override doors.
- **Unknown posture (the provider answers nothing): unchanged, right per answer A.** The predicate answers "no wall".
- **Platform administrator and system context: unchanged, right.** Both arms return before the new line.
- **A request that carries an organization: unchanged, right.** The comparison is the old one, with the null arm removed.
- **Public surface: none moved.** No export, schema key or `IApprovalService` member changes. `organizationWallStands` is private. The new runtime import of `normalizeTenancyPosture` and `postureEnforcesWall` comes from a package already in `dependencies`.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` is the level AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 prescribes. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. That is the right arm for an accept-set that only shrinks.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- The changeset carries the **BREAKING** banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, who moves, and the fix. The fix was checked against the tree: `os migrate organization-ownership` takes `--apply --plan-file --backup-taken`, and the ceremony's inventory lists `sys_approval_request` with fate attribution.
- The PR body carries the `Skills-docs:` line a narrowing owes.
- `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question, answer A (an unknown posture reads as unwalled): answered, holds.**
  - It matches `vetOrganizationClaim` for an absent posture, and ADR-0131 D9's lean-embedding note (no organization object, no wall).
  - The real tenancy service always answers a valid posture.
  - The package's existing harnesses construct the service with no provider and no request organization, so A is pinned incidentally.
- **The other `isOverrideActor` callers: answered by reading, not measured.**
  - The shared resolver states that with no active organization, no organization-scoped grant applies. The `TENANT_ADMIN` rung derives only from such a grant.
  - So a tenant-administrator context without a tenant does not come out of the shared resolver; only a hand-built context can carry it. The new denial runs in the wall's own direction. [detail held by the security seat]
  - It stays unpinned and absent from the changeset: a should-fix, in ④.
- **Changeset level `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: answered, right** (②).
- **Dogfood battery not measured: ESCALATED; CI does not answer it.**
  - The run on this head is a `pull_request` run. `Dogfood Regression Gate (${{ matrix.shard }}/3)` and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are `skipped` by design (AGENTS.md "Two speeds"), and the green `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate counted no shard.
  - No check-run on this head executed the new dogfood case, or any other dogfood file.
  - So the case is unmeasured everywhere, and by reading it cannot pass (④, must-fix).

### ④ Design judgment

**Against the spec, the narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real.**
- ADR-0131 D1 says NULL is not a state, and nothing reads a NULL tenant value as an owner. The removed arm read a NULL organization as "every organization's administrator".
- D9 stamps or refuses new writes, so the affected rows are those on stores built before the tenant column became NOT NULL.
- No declared capability is taken from a consumer: the override was only ever declared "within their own org".

Attempts to break it:
- **A door that still admits: none found.** All nine act doors reach `refuseUnreadableRequest`, directly or through `loadPendingRow`. The action-token and SLA paths run as the system by design. The record-lock hooks have no administrator bypass. The `admin_rescue` slate answers nobody for a request with no organization.
- **Over-refusal: none found.** The platform administrator and the system return before the new line. An organization's own administrator on its own request takes the unchanged comparison.
  - One consequence, which the changeset states: under a wall, an organization's administrator can no longer release their own record locked by a request with no organization. Only the platform administrator or the system can, until the ceremony attributes the row.
- **`single` changed: no.**
- **A refusal that differs from a missing id's: none found.** The throw is the same `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` with the caller's id. The validations that run before the row load are the same for both ids.
- **List and read paths beyond the ruling: one.** See should-fix 2 below.

Findings:

1. **Must-fix: the new dogfood case cannot plant its fixture on the harness store.**
   - The case sets `organization_id` to null on `sys_approval_request` through `driver.update`, on a fresh `bootStack` in-memory SQLite store.
   - On that store the driver creates the tenant column NOT NULL (ADR-0131 D1 note; `createColumn` with `tenantColumn`), and `sys_approval_request` declares `organization_id` with tenancy on.
   - `main`'s own QA checklist (`approvals.json`, knownGaps) records that exact UPDATE refused with `NOT NULL constraint failed`.
   - Sibling suites on the same harness relax the column first with `relaxTenantColumns` (`pre-18-tenant-column.testkit.ts`), for example `sharing-rule-org-less-caller.dogfood.test.ts`. This case does not.
   - This is a reading, not a run: no local run and no check-run on this head has executed the file. So the door-level claim in the PR body rests on nothing measured, and the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` would go red in the queue.
   - Fix: relax the tenant column on the approval tables before planting, and report a measured green run of the file on the new head.
2. **Should-fix: the read-side consequence is neither declared nor pinned.** The same line narrows the list, read and pending-approver-grant answers for a tenant-administrator context with no active organization under a wall. Add one pin per caller on a hand-built context, and one sentence in the changeset.
3. **Nit: the docblock overstates agreement with `vetOrganizationClaim`.** `organizationWallStands` normalizes the posture, so an unrecognized non-empty string reads as unwalled, while `vetOrganizationClaim` reads the same string as walled. The two agree only for an absent posture. The real tenancy service never emits such a value.
4. **Nit: the list-door pin does not discriminate.** It stays green under the ablation, because the list's organization filter already excluded the row. It is a control, not a pin of this change.
5. **Nit: a stale statement of the old rule.** `approval-revise.test.ts` still says "a null-org request is global". That now holds only without a wall.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-xpg7`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c7b9148bfac394b306e1db1e864fb66082208ece`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-revise.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-act-doors-read-visibility.dogfood.test.ts + packages/qa/dogfood/test/pre-18-tenant-column.testkit.ts, packages/core/src/security/system-write-organization.ts, packages/objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/pending-approver-read-grant.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md (all read on `main` or at the head, none reviewed)

This is a delta review of `350bc40b6e..c7b9148bfa` (commits 24b6c9a58c and c7b9148bfa) against the FAIL record on `350bc40b6e`. It also reads the replaced PR body and the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept-set or public-surface change is in the delta. The guard line in `isOverrideActor` and `organizationWallStands` are byte-identical to the reviewed head; the only source change is one docblock. Every judgment in ① of the prior record stands.

- **New pins for the three caller-organization readers: right.** A hand-built tenant-administrator context with no active organization is pinned under `isolated` and `group` on three readers: the data door's request visibility, the approvals list and the pending-approver read grant. Each has a `single` control. Each walled pin would have read the opposite before the guard line, so the pins discriminate.
- **Fake-engine `$null` arm: right.** It matches the fence the read grant spells for a caller with no organization.
- **`requestVisibilitySourceOf`: no surface moved.** It is an existing export the plugin already consumes.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right:
- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`;
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset;
- the BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker, and the `Skills-docs:` line.

`Lint & Repo Gates` is `success` on this head. `Check Changeset` was `success` on this head; its re-run after the body replacement was still in progress at the read, and it is advisory.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Answer A (an unknown posture reads as unwalled): still answered.** The docblock now says exactly where it agrees with `vetOrganizationClaim` (an absent posture), and that an unrecognised value reads as absent.
- **The other `isOverrideActor` callers: closed.** They are pinned and stated in the changeset. The prior reading stands: the shared resolver does not produce this context.
- **Changeset level: answered, right** (②).
- **Dogfood: answered by the dev's reading, not by CI.**
  - This head's run is again a `pull_request` run. The dogfood shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are `skipped` by design, and the green `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate counted no shard.
  - The measurement is the dev's local run under the verify lock, as the PR body reports it: the file 6 of 6, and the full battery 445 files passed, 3 skipped, exit 0.
  - The queue build is the first CI leg that will run it.
- **New fact (under a wall, the admitted administrator's decision write is refused by ADR-0131 D9): answered, true of the tree, not introduced here.**
  - The engine refuses an organization-less system write under a walled posture without asking the database anything (`system-write-organization.ts` on `main`).
  - Every act door inserts its action row before it touches the request row. So "nothing is written" holds on every door by reading, not only on approve, where it is pinned.
  - The refusal predates this PR and applied to every caller the old override admitted. The PR therefore removes no decision that could have landed at a real engine under a wall.

### ④ Design judgment

Prior findings:

1. **must-fix (the dogfood fixture could not be planted): closed.**
   - The case now relaxes the tenant column on the three approval tables with `relaxTenantColumns` before planting, the same door the sibling suites use.
   - The platform-administrator control no longer asserts a decision that cannot land. It pins not-unseen, `500 APPROVAL_APPROVE_FAILED` naming `sys_approval_action`, and an unchanged snapshot.
   - Closed by reading plus the dev's reported green run; no check-run on this head executed it.
2. **should-fix (the read-side consequence was undeclared and unpinned): closed.** Nine pins and one changeset sentence.
3. **nit (the docblock overstated agreement with `vetOrganizationClaim`): closed.**
4. **nit (the list-door pin does not discriminate): open, still a nit.** Unchanged in the delta.
5. **nit (a stale statement of the old rule in `approval-revise.test.ts`): closed.**

New public text against the tree:

- **Changeset body: true.** These statements all match the code read: "Only a platform administrator or a system context is admitted", "not decided at the door", "nothing is written", and "no door decides such a request under a walled posture". The ceremony is the right remedy: its inventory attributes `sys_approval_request`, `sys_approval_action` and `sys_approval_approver`, and the command line matches the CLI.
- **The narrowing against ADR-0131 D1 and D9: holds.** It still makes the spec's own refusal real, and the new text states D9's consequence instead of promising an act the engine refuses. The stuck request under a wall is D9's existing outcome; [detail held by the security seat].

New findings, none affecting correctness or the contract:

- **nit: "acts on" survives where only admission holds.** Several places still say the administrator acts: the PR title, the changeset's headline line, the `isOverrideActor` docblock and inline comment, and the unit control titles ("a platform administrator still acts on …" under a walled posture). Under a wall at a real engine, the administrator is admitted and the write is refused. The unit controls pin admission on an engine double that has no D9.
- **nit: the PR body's READ_BACK_FAILED note is loose.** It says the write lands for a platform administrator on a request with no organization, without limiting that to `single`.
- **nit: the PR body's two-minute check says 96 cases.** By reading, the file holds 99: 90 at the prior head plus the nine new pins. `Test Core` is `success` on this head either way.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f89aa1cf9e8eac7f80d99a8f7de0c39df065732a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-revise.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-act-doors-read-visibility.dogfood.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (read at the head, not reviewed)

This is a sync-delta review of `c7b9148bfa..f89aa1cf9e`. The head is a two-parent merge of `main` at `7e8b31ce5d` into `c7b9148bfa`, with no edit of its own. Its conclusions rest on a reading of the merged tree; CI on this head had not concluded (③).

### ① Derived judgments

The guard holds as judged on `c7b9148bfa`. The merged `isOverrideActor` and `organizationWallStands` were read at the head.

- **Order is unchanged.** System returns first, then the platform administrator. Next a caller that is not a tenant administrator is refused, then the null-organization arm runs, then the own-organization comparison.
- **The tenant-rung computation still runs before the null-organization arm.** `holdsTenantAdminRung(this.engine, held)` only decides who reaches that arm. Main narrowed its name read to the platform's own set, so the same callers or fewer reach the arm, never more.
- **The wall check gates the tenant arm only.** `organizationWallStands` has one caller, inside the tenant arm. Its body is byte-identical to the reviewed head.
- **Platform administrator and system still return first.** Main changed only how the platform name read is spelled; the posture arm is untouched.
- **The PR's net hunks in `approval-service.ts` against `main` are the same three as before:** the import, the docblock, and the guard line with its helper. Main's edits sit beside them, not inside them.
- **No other PR file moved in the merge.** The changeset, both test files and the dogfood file are identical to `c7b9148bfa`.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the banner and ADR-0087 marker as judged. The merge does not touch the changeset file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **All four dev flags stand as answered on `c7b9148bfa`.** The reading behind the caller-organization flag was re-checked at this head. The shared resolver still applies an organization-scoped grant only in its own organization, and still derives the tenant-administrator rung from such a grant.
- **Check-runs on this head had not concluded.** At the time of reading, 24 runs were listed:
  - `Governed Surface Queue Guard` was `success`.
  - The lint and type-check jobs, `filter`, `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards were in progress.
  - `Test Core`, `Build Core` and the other required contexts had not yet appeared.

  This record does not stand in for them. The seat must read the required contexts green on this head before arming.
- **CI still has not measured the dogfood case**, as on every `pull_request` run. The dev's local reading was taken on `c7b9148bfa`, not on this merge. The queue build is the first leg that runs it on merged code.

### ④ Design judgment

Nothing main brought in reopens a finding.

- **The prior must-fix and should-fix stay closed.** The files that closed them are unchanged.
- **Main's change composes with the narrowing.** It restricts the administrator name reads to the platform's own sets; [detail held by the security seat]. It widens no arm, and the same predicate still feeds the `admin_rescue` slate.
- **The narrowing holds against ADR-0131 D1 and D9, as judged.**
- **One exposure to watch in CI, not a finding.** The PR's unit pins resolve the tenant administrator through the real resolver, which main changed. Whether they stay green on merged code is `Test Core`'s verdict on this head, which is not yet in.
- **Open nits carried over, unchanged:**
  - the list-door pin does not discriminate;
  - "acts on" survives in the title, headline and docblock where only admission holds;
  - the PR body's case count and its READ_BACK_FAILED note.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · head `f89aa1cf9e8eac7f80d99a8f7de0c39df065732a` · 2026-11-10T11:44Z

- **Shape:** 4 files. Not governed. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Patch for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, with the BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker.
- **Contract review** at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, one isolated reviewer:
  - Full record on `350bc40b6e`, comment 6762271297: FAIL. The dogfood fixture could not be planted, and the read-side consequence was undeclared.
  - Delta record on `c7b9148bfa`, comment 6766001968: PASS. Both findings are closed.
  - Sync-delta record on this head, comment 6766060528: PASS. The guard holds in the merged `isOverrideActor`, and main's change only narrows who reaches the arm. Its condition was that `Test Core` pass on this head, and it now reads `success`.
- **Rule held** (ruling of record 6755714726 on #32004; ADR-0131 D1):
  - Under walled postures, only a platform administrator or the system is admitted to act on an approval request that has no organization. Any other administrator is answered exactly as for a missing id. Under the `single` posture nothing changes.
  - Under a wall, such a request is not decided at any door, because ADR-0131 D9 refuses its action write. The remedy is the voluntary `os migrate organization-ownership` ceremony, which the changeset names.
